nws.title: Weather Service watches and warnings
nws.detail: Nothing for Western New York right now.

ao.title: Arctic Oscillation: is cold air escaping?
ao.detail: Model average goes as low as -0.6 (Dec 7) and as high as +1.2. Below -2 = cold air can escape south. Above +2.5 = cold stays up north.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation: is cold air steered our way?
nao.detail: Model average goes as low as +0.1 (Dec 11) and as high as +1.0. Below -1.5 = cold air gets steered into the East.

cpc610.title: NOAA 6–10 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc610.detail: Dec 3–Dec 7: 80% chance of being warmer than normal.

cpc814.title: NOAA 8–14 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc814.detail: Dec 5–Dec 11: 80% chance of being warmer than normal.

erie.title: Lake Erie water temperature
erie.detail: Nov 26: 6°F warmer than normal (47°F). Record for the date: 52.6°F (2024). Warmer water = more fuel for lake-effect snow.

vortex.title: Will the polar vortex break down?
vortex.detail: In 0 of 31 runs of the American weather model, the spinning winds over the Arctic stop and reverse within 28 days. That can send Arctic air south 1 to 3 weeks later. Yesterday: 0%.

noreaster.title: Nor'easter in the next 10 days?
noreaster.detail: 30 of 31 model runs show a strong storm off the Northeast coast around Nov 30. Strongest run: 979 mb (lower = stronger).

freeze.title: First freeze in Buffalo
freeze.detail: Buffalo first hit 32°F on Nov 24. Coldest run: 27°F.

arctic.title: Arctic air over Buffalo?
arctic.detail: 2 of 31 model runs bring air colder than 14°F about 5,000 ft up around Dec 7. Coldest run: 11°F up there.

lakeeffect.title: Lake-effect snow setup?
lakeeffect.detail: 31 of 31 model runs get cold enough over Lake Erie (53°F water) for lake-effect snow around Dec 1. 100% show lake-effect rain showers.

seiche.title: Lake Erie seiche (sloshing) now
seiche.detail: Buffalo water level minus Toledo: +0.9 ft (Buffalo 2.6 ft above low water). 6+ ft difference = a big seiche.

waves.title: Lake Erie waves now
waves.detail: Eastern Lake Erie buoy: 0.0 ft waves. 8+ ft = big wave day.

aurora.title: Northern lights in the next 3 days?
aurora.detail: Highest forecast: Kp 3.0 around Nov 29. Kp 6+ = maybe visible from WNY, 7+ = good chance.

storms.title: Thunderstorm photo days
storms.detail: No thunderstorms expected in the next 3 days.

seichewind.title: Seiche / big-wave wind coming?
seichewind.detail: 2 of 31 model runs blow SW winds of 35+ mph down Lake Erie around Dec 7. Strongest run: 42 mph.

seasmoke.title: Sea smoke (lake steam) mornings
seasmoke.detail: Needs Buffalo at 23°F or colder over 53°F water. 0 of 31 model runs get there in the next 10 days.

fallsice.title: Niagara Falls ice?
fallsice.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring 3 straight nights at 10°F or colder in the next 10 days.

recent.text: 🌀 Nor'easter signal. A nor'easter is a strong storm that spins up off the East Coast and pulls in wind, rain and snow from the northeast. In 22 of 31 runs of the American weather model (71%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 28. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 976 mb.

🌊 Lake Erie seiche happening now. Strong wind is pushing the lake's water toward Toledo, like water sloshing to one end of a bathtub. Buffalo's water is 6.1 feet lower than Toledo's right now. The Buffalo shoreline is drained: exposed lakebed and shipwreck-hunting photos.

In 27 of 31 runs of the American weather model (87%), that happens over Lake Erie around Nov 12. Wind direction decides who gets buried.
